first.text:
Practically, nothing in your sessions changes. Wednesday is still 3 sets of negatives and 4 sets of band pull-ups, Sunday still adds 3 band sets, Friday still opens with the one strict test rep. Same loads, same bands, same cues.

What changes is how the week is judged afterwards:

- **The pull-up gets a real score.** Until now the weekly read on the pull-up was "1 of 1" because only the strict single counted, which told us nothing. From now on the negatives and band sets count toward a target of 10 hard sets a week. A full week lands at 11; lose Wednesday and it reads 4, and that shows up as the pull-up falling behind instead of disappearing.
- **A short pattern gets caught.** If the pull-up work comes in under 10 in three weeks out of four, I'm prompted to act: add a set, move a set to another day, or ask what's getting in the way. Before this change that signal couldn't fire.
- **A disrupted week protects it.** When illness or travel cuts a week down to the minimum, each of the five lifts keeps at least two hard sets. For the pull-up, negatives or band sets now satisfy that, so a trimmed week won't try to fill the slot with extra strict singles you can't do yet.

What it does not do: the negatives and band work don't replace the strict rep, they don't get tested, and they don't have to come first in a session. The Friday single stays the measure, and strict sets become real work once that rep passes about five, as before.

So the day-to-day is identical; the difference is that the weekly report will finally tell us the truth about your pull-up volume. Still ready to record it on your yes.
